knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A toolbox talk is useful because it is brief, regular and tied to real work.
An alert earns attention when it matches a hazard the crew meets in its own work.
Each agreed action is recorded and checked at the next talk until it is closed.

practicalCriteria: The learner runs a ten-minute toolbox talk on a supplied work topic, with each attendee invited to speak.
The learner completes the talk record and posts a matching alert, with the posting date recorded.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed talk record and posted alert
stopWorkCriteria: Stop the work and refer to the supervisor where a hazard raised in a talk cannot be controlled with the crew's current procedure.
Stop and refer any product whose instructions are not available on site.
